messages:
raj: spun up new SCL1 cluster (8x A100s) for the Latency/Throughput validation run — want kernel/driver sanity, nvlink checks, and a p95 baseline for gen2 workloads. I kicked off the perf harness at /infra/perf/scl1/run-2026-03-18. Can folks run quick sanity and post results here?

maria: on it. starting with driver/module checks and dmesg. will run nvidia-smi + simple kernel version compare.

maria: command I ran:
```
ssh ops@scl1-provisioner
modinfo nvidia | egrep -i "version|alias"
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
```

maria: output shows driver 525.85.* on host, container images reference 530.*. that mismatch could explain some nvlink init warnings I saw in dmesg. copying snippets: 
```
[  12.345678] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[  12.346789] nvidia: version magic '5.15.0-112-generic' should be '5.15.0-110-rt'
[  12.347000] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
[  12.350000] nvidia-mig: NVMLInit failed: 13
```

dana: thanks @maria. I ran the perf harness for a 512-token generation workload (batch=1, no caching) — p95 token latency looks higher than our baseline:
- expected p95 single-token stage ~45ms
- observed p95 single-token stage ~62ms
- sustained throughput (tokens/sec) ~7200 vs expected ~9500 for same model on other regions

sam: saw similar. also noticed packet drops between nodes during the soak run. checked iperf between two GPU nodes — small bursts of retransmits. suspect MTU mismatch on the overlay.

sam: iperf snippet:
```
iperf3 -c 10.2.5.12 -P 4 -t 30
[  4]  0.00-30.00 sec  2.45 GBytes  702 Mbits/sec  0.12 ms  (summary)
[SUM]  0.00-30.00 sec 19.6 GBytes  5.62 Gbits/sec  10.2 ms  retransmits=84
```

leo: MTU/overlay mismatch makes sense — the cluster network vendor defaults to 1500 on leaf switches here, but our overlay (flannel/eni) expects 9000. this will add encapsulation and fragmentation. I put a quick patch to set mtu=8950 on kube-cni DaemonSet in staging. recommend we redeploy and re-run.

raj: good catch. @ops-bot can you apply the kube-cni config change in the perf cluster and roll one node at a time? We need minimal disruption but also fresh NV driver probe after change.

ops-bot: ack. scheduling rolling update for kube-cni DaemonSet on scl1 nodes. one node cordon/drain at a time. ETA ~12 minutes.

ops-bot: kube-cni update completed on node-01..node-08, all pods back up.

maria: re-ran dmesg/driver checks post-mtu change. nvlink init warnings reduced but still a stray NVMLInit call failing on node-03 during container startup. suspect container runtime is using an older nvidia-container-runtime. checking the container runtime plugin versions now.

maria: nvidia-container-runtime versions:
```
root@node-03:~# nvidia-container-cli -V
nvidia-container-cli: 1.11.0
root@node-03:~# apt list --installed | grep nvidia-container-toolkit
ii  nvidia-container-toolkit 1.13.0
```

maria: we have a mismatch (cli 1.11 vs toolkit 1.13) — will align them to 1.13 across nodes and reboot the kubelet on node-03.

dana: after aligning runtimes and MTU fix, I re-ran the same perf harness. new numbers: p95 single-token stage ~47ms, sustained throughput ~9200 tokens/sec. much closer to baseline. PNG: quick table I pasted to artifacts.

sam: network retransmits dropped to near-zero after MTU fix. iperf now: 5.5 Gbits/sec with retransmits=2.

leo: kernel/driver reconciliation note: we should pin host driver to 525.85.* and update any container base images to use matching cuda/driver stacks. I'll open a follow-up PR in infra-images to retire references to 530 tags for scl1 images.

raj: TL;DR: initial regressions caused by two small issues: 1) MTU/overlay mismatch adding fragmentation, 2) container/runtime driver mismatch on one node. fixes applied: mtu -> 8950, runtime/toolkit aligned to 1.13, rebooted kubelet on node-03. perf now within 5% of east/west baseline.

raj: handoff to oncall for final soak and signoff: @eng-oncall please run a 2-hour soak with mixed batch sizes (1/4/8) and report any regressions. I'd like cost/throughput notes too — looks like we should prefer reserved scheduling for these nodes due to spot reclamation risks in the region.

ops-bot: soak job scheduled: perf-soak/scl1/2h/mixed-batches — started. logs available at https://internal.perf.redwood/scl1/soak/1890202020.

sam: quick cost note — spot availability in SCL fluctuates. for predictable tail-latency workloads we'll recommend dedicated pools or convertible reserved nodes. will draft a short cost comparison doc after soak finishes. :money_with_wings:

leo: creating infra-images PR shortly. tagging @dana for model-config changes if any further tuning needed.

dana: thanks all — if soak is clean, we can admit scl1 into dedicated pool inventory next week. otherwise we'll iterate on kernel/driver pinning and network overlay params. :thumbsup:
